    AI Overview
    The Dow is down, entering correction territory (down 10% from its February peak), driven primarily by surging oil prices above
    a barrel due to the escalating conflict in Iran, which threatens to increase inflation. Investor anxiety over persistent geopolitical risks, supply chain disruption, and potential interest rate hikes to counter energy-driven inflation has triggered widespread selling. 
    Key Factors Driving the Downturn: 
    • Energy Prices & Geopolitics: The ongoing conflict with Iran has driven oil prices over
      per barrel, sparking fears of sustained energy inflation and global supply disruption.
    • Correction Territory:
      The Dow has fallen into a correction—dropping roughly 10% from its February 10 record high of over
      .
    • Inflation Concerns: Rising energy costs and uncertainty are creating fears of higher long-term inflation and stagflation, making investors nervous about the economic outlook.
    • Corporate Concerns: Specific stocks, such as UnitedHealth, have weighed on the index following regulatory investigations.
    • Volatile Markets: Even with recent remarks from Fed Chair Powell downplaying immediate inflation risks, investors remain cautious about the impact of a protracted conflict. 
    The market continues to react to the potential for further military action in the Middle East and its subsequent impact on economic growth.

      As of the close on Monday, March 30, 2026, the
      Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell by 0.73% to finish at 20,794.64, driven by a decline in chip stocks and rising oil prices. Tech-heavy stocks and semiconductor manufacturers, including Micron and SanDisk, faced pressure, leading the index to drop from earlier gains. 
      Key Details for Monday, March 30, 2026: 
      • Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC): 20,794.64 (-0.73%)
      • Day's Range: 20,690.25 - 21,139.72
      • Context: The market experienced a weak session as oil prices surged past $100 per barrel and investors worried about inflation. 
      Top Influencers and Sectors: 
      • Chip Stocks Slide: Micron Technology and SanDisk fell significantly.
      • Oil Prices: Continued to rally, affecting market sentiment.
      • Market Trend: The Nasdaq has been under pressure, with this marking a continuation of recent volatility. 
      Note: The market will be closed this Friday for the Good Friday holiday.

      Description

      The NASDAQ Composite is a stock market index that includes almost all stocks listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Along with the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500, it is one of the three most-followed stock market indices in the United States. Wikipedia

      Market cap: US$35.3 trillion; (as of September 2025)
      Related indices: Nasdaq-100
      Trading symbol: ^IXIC.IXIC; COMP
      Weighting method: Capitalization-weighted index
